papers.title: Knsight: Self-Evolving Agentic System for Production Cloud Root Cause Analysis
papers.abstract: Cloud incident response increasingly relies on LLM agents that translate heterogeneous telemetry and natural-language alerts into operator-facing diagnoses. However, in production RCA workflows, LLM agents commonly serialize these structured signals into text, losing the temporal and topological structure that is critical for diagnosis. We present Knsight, an industry-deployed RCA agent that converts operational telemetry into chart-image canvases and uses a frozen multimodal LLM to reason directly over visual evidence. Knsight introduces Vision Recursive-of-Thought (V-RoT), an iterative diagnose-review-refine loop in which a Reviewer module inspects each canvas and decides whether to refine, zoom in, or stop. To adapt across recurring production failures, Knsight further converts Reviewer feedback into a shared, alias-substituted skill library used at inference time. Offline, on the OpenRCA benchmark, Knsight improves aggregate Correct by 7.0 points over the strongest text-only baseline and reduces timeouts from 117 to 11. Online, in a 90-day deployment across 1,284 production incidents, Knsight increases top-1 acceptance from 38.9% to 71.4% and reduces time-to-acknowledge and time-to-resolve by 59% and 32%, respectively.
papers.reason: 图像画布是诊断智能体的核心交互界面：Reviewer 根据画布决定细化、放大或停止，并将反馈转化为推理时复用的技能。相比纯文本基线，端到端结果支持整体设计，但未单独验证视觉循环或技能库的贡献。
papers.evidence: Knsight introduces Vision Recursive-of-Thought (V-RoT), an iterative diagnose-review-refine loop in which a Reviewer module inspects each canvas and decides whether to refine, zoom in, or stop.
papers.result: Offline, on the OpenRCA benchmark, Knsight improves aggregate Correct by 7.0 points over the strongest text-only baseline and reduces timeouts from 117 to 11.

papers.title: Tool-Making and Self-Evolving LLM Agents in Low-Latency Systems
papers.abstract: Production LLM agents often waste latency and reliability by regenerating code for the same procedural steps on every request. We replace this inference-time coding loop with an agentic tool-making pipeline that compiles repeated SOP steps into validated, versioned tools before deployment. The tool-maker grounds synthesis in the live environment as it collects execution traces, observes backend schemas and values, generates candidate tools, and repairs them against labeled cases. At runtime, the production agent calls these tools directly and falls back to code generation only when needed. We deploy the approach in a Fulfillment Center alarm-triage system, where an agent diagnoses alarms against a 44-node SOP over heterogeneous metric backends. In production, tool calls reduce p50 latency by 42%. On 1500 historical alarms, they reduce end-to-end error rate by up to 53% by suppressing run-to-run variance in repeated steps. Because tools return compact structured verdicts, they also enable a simpler direct-call architecture, reducing p50 latency by a further 62% in a controlled ablation. Versioned tools also improve auditability and expose specification gaps and upstream data drift. Our results show that agents that build and maintain their own tool libraries, a key element of self-evolving agents, can make industrial LLM systems faster, more reliable, and easier to operate.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是让软件代理利用真实执行轨迹和带标签的测试反馈，生成、修复并维护可复用的版本化工具，以替代逐请求写代码。跨模型组件消融、留出集测试和生产对照支持其效果；残余错误分析明确了规范质量的限制，但跨业务泛化尚未验证。另有基于筛选轨迹的辅助微调，并验证了无工具时的回退能力。工具上线仍需人工审核，未展示改进机制自身的演化。
papers.evidence: We replace this inference-time coding loop with an agentic tool-making pipeline that compiles repeated SOP steps into validated, versioned tools before deployment.
papers.result: In production, tool calls reduce p50 latency by 42%.

papers.title: Learning What Not to Forget: Long-Horizon Agent Memory from a Few Kilobytes of Learning
papers.abstract: Long-running language-model systems accumulate interaction history that outgrows the context window, so they must continually evict. When an eviction policy drops a task-critical detail, for example an access token issued at login or a path the next call needs, the action fails. We present LRE (Learned Relevance Eviction), a kilobyte-scale, CPU-only, language-model-free scorer that learns which units of history are task-critical and keeps them by verbatim extraction. Under a matched-budget comparison, in our experiment, no baseline dominates LRE on the accuracy-cost plane. On agents, LRE recovers 93% of the aggregate accuracy of keeping the entire history (41.1 vs. 44.0) and exceeds it by 27% on the simplest tasks, while requiring zero compressor calls and cutting the worst-case peak prompt by 52%. A controlled study trace shows LRE completes tasks where the others loop, finishing one such task in 37% fewer calls than keeping everything and solving 14 tasks where no other run policy does. On conversational memory, LRE outranks dense and token-pruning encoders at zero neural cost while being 295–1569× smaller in size. In downstream evaluation, LRE gives the best budgeted answer quality on LoCoMo reading 68% fewer tokens. Its supervision can also be annotation-free: training only on the system’s own behavior recovers 95% of the supervised scorer’s effectiveness. We argue that, because memory eviction in LLM agents is a fidelity problem, it requires a deployable proactive policy where the future query is unavailable and exact state is decisive, and that cheap learned relevance can be sufficient.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是用轻量学习式评分器主动淘汰交互历史，逐字保留影响后续行动的关键信息。在未来查询未知的条件下，等预算对照量化了任务准确率与提示开销之间的取舍；摘要未给出足以复现评分器的细节。
papers.evidence: We present LRE (Learned Relevance Eviction), a kilobyte-scale, CPU-only, language-model-free scorer that learns which units of history are task-critical and keeps them by verbatim extraction.
papers.result: On agents, LRE recovers 93% of the aggregate accuracy of keeping the entire history (41.1 vs. 44.0) and exceeds it by 27% on the simplest tasks, while requiring zero compressor calls and cutting the worst-case peak prompt by 52%.

papers.title: AdaMem: Learning What to Remember with Adaptive Memory Policies for Personalized Agents
papers.abstract: Long-term memory systems allow LLM agents to preserve information beyond a single context window, but most systems focus on storing and retrieving facts after extraction, leaving the write decision under-specified. What deserves memory can depend on the user’s current task, topic, activity, or interaction partner, while uniform extraction applies one notion of importance across these different situations. We formulate this challenge as preference-conditioned write control and introduce AdaMem, which uses adaptive natural-language Memory Policies to personalize what an agent writes to memory. Each policy represents the user’s memory preference for a particular interaction context, is updated from periodic feedback, and controls subsequent memory writing. We evaluate this loop in AdaMem-Bench, which assigns different memory preferences to six concurrent interaction personas across five ten-week stories. Across two extraction models and two feedback modes, AdaMem improves average QA accuracy over Mem0 from 80.0% to 84.35% while reducing persistent memory by 9.27%. Our analyses show that explicit feedback helps models learn better memory policies, but current models still struggle to translate those policies into reliably selective writing behavior. AdaMem thus demonstrates the promise of adaptive write control while exposing policy execution as a central limitation of current memory agents. Our code is publicly available.[<https://github.com/galaxyChen/AdaMem>]
papers.reason: 核心贡献是用按交互情境区分、随周期性反馈更新的自然语言策略控制长期记忆写入。相较 Mem0，平均问答准确率从 80.0% 提升至 84.35%，持久记忆减少 9.27%。结果支持将写入策略与信息抽取分开设计，但模型仍难以可靠地执行选择性写入。
papers.evidence: We formulate this challenge as preference-conditioned write control and introduce AdaMem, which uses adaptive natural-language Memory Policies to personalize what an agent writes to memory.
papers.result: Across two extraction models and two feedback modes, AdaMem improves average QA accuracy over Mem0 from 80.0% to 84.35% while reducing persistent memory by 9.27%.

papers.title: CapMem: A Benchmark for Caption-Based Episodic Memory in Egocentric Video
papers.abstract: Wearable assistants require episodic memory over egocentric video, yet current vision-language models face bounded frame budgets, growing visual-token costs, and long-context retrieval failures. Under these practical constraints, we study whether textual captions can serve as reusable episodic memory. We define the Episodic Memory Video Caption QA task and introduce CapMem, a human-annotated benchmark with 75 videos totaling 33.7 hours, and 1,000 multiple-choice questions across 16 scenarios. On long videos (>20 min), full-coverage CaptionQA with 30s and 60s caption windows outperforms direct VideoQA for 10/12 and 8/12 models, respectively. On the same video subset, a matched-frame control across six Qwen models retains mean accuracy gains of 3.22 and 2.55 points, respectively. Our caption-guided retrieve-and-verify harness further improves accuracy by up to 5.3 points. These results support the effectiveness of caption memory for episodic reasoning over long egocentric video.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是评估可穿戴助手如何复用第一视角视频的情景记忆，而非设计摄像系统。方法将视频分段转为带时间戳的描述，并在检索后用稀疏帧核验。等帧对照显示，超过20分钟的视频中，30秒窗口平均提升3.22个百分点；短视频上直接视频问答通常更强，且受控结果限于Qwen模型。
papers.evidence: We define the Episodic Memory Video Caption QA task and introduce CapMem, a human-annotated benchmark
papers.result: On the same video subset, a matched-frame control across six Qwen models retains mean accuracy gains of 3.22 and 2.55 points, respectively.

papers.title: TSHMem: A Temporal-Semantic Hierarchical Memory Graph for Long-Term Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: Long-term conversational agents often face time-sensitive queries, requiring evidence that is both contextually relevant and valid for a specific time, event, or factual update. However, noisy temporal-entity cues, weak coupling between temporal anchors and retrieval paths, and sparse long-tail evidence often lead memory systems to retrieve semantically similar but temporally invalid or outdated evidence. We propose TSHMem, a Temporal-Semantic Hierarchical Memory Graph for long-term conversational agents. TSHMem addresses noisy conversational evidence by organizing dialogue turns, self-contained statements, hierarchical summaries, and entities into a heterogeneous memory graph. To connect temporal constraints with retrieval paths, it parses temporal intent, activates query-relevant entities, resolves event-referenced constraints, and injects temporal relevance into graph transition probabilities. It then combines time-aware structural propagation with semantic matching and hierarchical ranking to retrieve compact evidence that is temporally valid, contextually relevant, and robust to sparse long-tail memories. Experiments on LongMemEval S* and LoCoMo show that TSHMem consistently outperforms strong retrieval and memory-agent baselines, achieving 66.3% accuracy on LongMemEval S*, with an absolute gain of 18.6% over the strongest baseline while retrieving fewer evidence tokens.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是为长期对话代理构建外部记忆图，并将时间约束纳入图转移概率，以检索对当前查询仍然有效的历史证据。摘要报告了量化基线比较，但未提供消融、复现细节或适用边界。
papers.evidence: To connect temporal constraints with retrieval paths, it parses temporal intent, activates query-relevant entities, resolves event-referenced constraints, and injects temporal relevance into graph transition probabilities.
papers.result: achieving 66.3% accuracy on LongMemEval S*, with an absolute gain of 18.6% over the strongest baseline while retrieving fewer evidence tokens.

papers.title: MAViQ: Memory-Augmented Visual Querying for Multi-Turn MLLM Jailbreaks
papers.abstract: Jailbreaks against multimodal large language models (MLLMs) typically operate through image-text inputs. After each target response, the attacker must decide how the new feedback should shape the next image-text query: which clues should be stated in the text, which should appear as visual evidence, and how the text should refer to the image.Existing multimodal attacks typically rely on fixed image-text pairs or candidate search, limiting their ability to adapt across turns.Text-only multi-turn attacks can adapt to prior responses, but they do not decide how response-derived clues should be expressed across image and text.In this paper, we formulate this missing step as \textit{trace-to-query realization} and propose \underline{M}emory-\underline{A}ugmented \underline{Vi}sual \underline{Q}uerying (MAViQ), a black-box framework that converts response-derived clues into visual and textual constraints, refines the query after observing the generated image, and propagates feedback to subsequent turns.Extensive experiments on two benchmarks across six target MLLMs show that MAViQ achieves average attack success rates (ASRs) of 70.60% on MM-SafetyBench and 82.13% on JailbreakV-mini, outperforming the strongest baseline by 5.90% and 8.32%, respectively. Our code is available at  https://github.com/jixingtian/Maviq.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是利用跨轮反馈调整图文查询的交互框架，明确区别于固定图文对和仅文本的多轮方法。两个基准、六个目标模型的结果提供了量化基线比较，但摘要未报告消融，也未证明系统存储了图像记忆。
papers.evidence: we formulate this missing step as \textit{trace-to-query realization}
papers.result: outperforming the strongest baseline by 5.90% and 8.32%, respectively.

papers.title: COLLABMEM: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Collaborative Memory Operations in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly rely on persistent memory to coordinate role-specialized work. Correctness requires more than recalling a fact: the fact must reach the right role, remain hidden from unauthorized roles, carry the right source, and update when a more authoritative value appears. We introduce COLLABMEM, a diagnostic benchmark for collaborative memory operations. Its matched memory-only harness fixes the trace, target role, answerer, judge, and gold event, localizing errors to sharing, access, routing, provenance, conflict resolution, or retention. COLLABMEM contains 58 hand-authored scenarios (1,118 core probes), a 174-scenario scaled split (3,359 probes), adversarial and compositional hard sets, and six transactive-memory competencies. We also propose TMS-GRAPH++, a scope-aware graph memory framework with role-filtered views, writer/provenance structure, and temporal [CURRENT] marking. Across five evaluation splits, TMS-GRAPH++ achieves the highest non-Oracle average score (69.6%). Evaluations using the official SDKs of Mem0, Letta, and A-Mem show that shared archives help, but reliable collaborative memory still requires explicit visibility, provenance, authority, and retention policies. We will release the dataset, evaluation code, and reproduced outputs to support future work on multi-agent memory systems.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是面向多智能体持久记忆的诊断基准。评测固定交互轨迹、目标角色、答题者、裁判和金标准事件，以定位共享、访问、路由、溯源、冲突消解和保留问题。所提图记忆在五个划分上的非 Oracle 平均分最高（69.6%），为显式设置可见性、来源、权威性和保留规则提供了设计依据；摘要未报告各机制的独立效果。
papers.evidence: We introduce COLLABMEM, a diagnostic benchmark for collaborative memory operations.
papers.result: Across five evaluation splits, TMS-GRAPH++ achieves the highest non-Oracle average score (69.6%).

papers.title: SWE-MEM: Learning Adaptive Memory Management for Long-Horizon Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon software engineering agents often need to manage lengthy and noisy interaction histories under limited context budgets. Existing memory management methods rely on static compression workflows or rigid compression schedules, and often decouple memory decisions from task-solving performance. We present SWE-MeM, a training framework for proactive and on-demand memory management in software engineering agents. SWE-MeM provides a flexible memory tool that lets agents decide when, what, and how to compress based on trajectory state, task progress, and remaining context budget. We train agents with synthesized proactive memory-management trajectories and Memory-aware GRPO, which jointly optimizes memory management and issue resolution through memory-aware trajectory splitting and step-level credit assignment. On SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-MeM achieves 43.4% and 60.2% resolve rate with 4B and 30B models, respectively, outperforming existing memory management baselines in both performance and efficiency.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是让软件工程智能体根据任务进度和上下文预算，自主决定何时压缩交互历史、保留什么以及如何压缩，以支持后续行动。摘要报告了解决率及相对基线的优势，但未提供消融或量化效率权衡。
papers.evidence: SWE-MeM provides a flexible memory tool that lets agents decide when, what, and how to compress based on trajectory state, task progress, and remaining context budget.
papers.result: On SWE-Bench Verified, SWE-MeM achieves 43.4% and 60.2% resolve rate with 4B and 30B models, respectively, outperforming existing memory management baselines in both performance and efficiency.

papers.title: AtomMem: Learnable Dynamic Agentic Memory with Atomic Memory Operation
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents increasingly face tasks that require reasoning over extremely long range. A key bottleneck is memory design: most prior approaches treat memory as a static, human-designed component, limiting adaptability. Inspired by biological memory evolution, we propose AtomMem, a framework that exposes a set of atomic memory operations—including summarization and CRUD primitives—as tool-like actions. The agent learns a policy over these operations purely via reinforcement learning, using only the task reward. AtomMem allows the agent to dynamically interleave summarization and CRUD to retain important information while managing memory efficiently. We evaluate AtomMem on streaming long-context understanding and web-navigation benchmarks, demonstrating an average improvement of 8.5 points over static memory workflows and 2.1 points over the current learnable-memory baseline. Ablation studies show that both summarization and CRUD are essential to train agent memory. The project can be accessed at https://github.com/RUCBM/AtomMem.
papers.reason: 核心贡献是让智能体学习何时用摘要和 CRUD 操作保留或修订外部记忆。两类基准上报告了相对静态及可学习基线的平均增益；摘要未给出消融效应量或适用边界。
papers.evidence: we propose AtomMem, a framework that exposes a set of atomic memory operations—including summarization and CRUD primitives—as tool-like actions.
papers.result: demonstrating an average improvement of 8.5 points over static memory workflows and 2.1 points over the current learnable-memory baseline.
